transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Next: Try an ordinary evenly-distributed load to rule out load imbalance. Let me know what you find.
It's not the load, it's every spin now. Gets louder the faster it spins, like a jet engine. Washes and drains fine though.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
It rumbles and grinds when I turn it. Doesn't feel smooth.

With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side. Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?
Yes there's a noticeable clunky up and down movement when I lift it at the edge. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on whether the noise persists when you run an empty spin cycle, as this will determine if the issue is caused by the load or a mechanical fault in the machine itself. Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?
Yes it spins when empty, it's still really loud on the spin though. Is it worth fixing?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. It depends on whether the noise is caused by a simple foreign object like a coin or bra wire trapped in the drum seal. If removing such an item resolves the issue, the repair is straightforward and worthwhile. Look all round the inside of the drum, under the paddles and in the folds of the door seal for a coin, bra wire or other object. Turn the drum slowly by hand and listen for anything sliding or catching. Did you find something and remove it, can you see or hear something stuck that you can't get out, or is there nothing there?
Can't see anything in the drum holes or between the drum and tub, no coins or wire. Is it worth fixing?

It is usually worth fixing if the noise is caused by remaining transit bolts, as removing them is a simple and inexpensive repair. If the bolts are already gone, the issue may involve more significant internal components like bearings or the suspension system. New machines come with transit (shipping) bolts in the back panel that lock the drum for delivery. If they're still in, it bangs on the spin. Are any transit bolts still fitted (and have you taken them out), or were they already removed?
[Helpful to see: image "Check the transit bolts have been removed" — Transit bolts hold the drum still for delivery and must be removed before use — a machine that bangs, walks or vibrates (especially when new or recently moved) often still has them fitted. They unscrew from the back of the machine. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
No, it's had them out for years, it's level and was fine before. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on whether the noise persists when you run a spin cycle with laundry inside, as this will help determine if the issue is related to unbalanced loads or a mechanical fault. Run a spin-only (or rinse and spin) programme with the washing in. Does the drum spin up properly on that programme?
I already did the empty spin and it spins fine, just very loud. Is it worth fixing? It's 9 years old and cost about £350 new.

It depends on whether the noise persists with an even load, as this could indicate a simple imbalance or a more serious mechanical fault like worn bearings. Given the appliance is nine years old and was originally inexpensive, significant repair costs may not be financially viable compared to replacement. Next: Try a normal, evenly-distributed load (and check the spin/programme setting isn't reduced/off). Let me know what you find.

tags.checkGiven: Now run a normal load with a spin. Is it spinning smoothly now, or does it still shake badly?
